title: An enemy brain
description:
Give an enemy states: patrol, chase when it sees the player, and give up after losing them.

```
patrol between (100, 200) and (300, 200)
player 80 px away -> CHASE
player out of sight for 3 s -> RETURN to the patrol path
back on the path -> PATROL
```
hints: Write the switch twice in your head: "what do I do in this state" and "when do I leave it" (lesson 4.04).
"Can see" is a distance test: `std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) < 120` with `dx = px - e.x` and `dy = py - e.y` (`std::hypot(dx, dy)` from `<cmath>` computes the same distance).
requirements: `enum class State { patrol, chase, search, returnHome }` with an `update(dt, playerPos)` that switches states.
Seeing means within 120 pixels; losing sight starts a 3-second timer in `search`.
Each state moves the enemy differently; print state changes only.
stretch: Use the path finder from lesson 4.05 for `returnHome` around walls.
